recent_posts.title: Embrace the monolith: Adding a new product to Aha!
recent_posts.summary: The post explores the options of starting a new product, either from a brand new codebase, microservices, or continuing with the existing monolithic codebase. It highlights the benefits of embracing the monolith and reusing existing code, as well as the challenges of implementing features and integrating with the billing system.

recent_posts.title: Ruby Weekly Issue 799: May 7, 2026
recent_posts.summary: Ruby Weekly issue 799 covers Ruby concurrency primitives (processes, Ractors, threads, fibers) with benchmarks and diagrams, a hot take on avoiding asset pipelines entirely, Rails tips on safe HTML helpers, RubyLLM 1.15.0 with image editing and cost tracking, and Fuik, a new webhook engine for Rails.

recent_posts.title: RubyLLM 1.15: Image Editing, Cost Tracking and Less Tool Boilerplate
recent_posts.summary: RubyLLM 1.15 ships several developer-experience improvements. Image editing is now supported via the existing `paint` method with a `with:` parameter accepting paths, URLs, IO objects, or Active Storage attachments, plus optional mask support. Cost tracking is built in — responses, chats, and agents now expose `.cost.total` calculated from the model registry without any custom code. Token counts are restructured to cleanly separate input, output, cache_read, and cache_write tokens. Tool boilerplate is reduced by inferring parameters from Ruby method signatures. Callbacks are now additive (multiple can stack) rather than replace-style, fixing conflicts between Rails persistence and app-level callbacks. Rails fixes include Action Text conversion, Zeitwerk eager-load compatibility, and Active Storage blob reuse. The model registry adds pricing for GPT Image, reasoning tokens, and new model aliases including Claude Opus 4.7, DeepSeek V4, Gemini Embedding 2, Gemma 4, and GPT-5.5.

recent_posts.title: Adding edit, delete and reposition for nested forms in Rails with Stimulus
recent_posts.summary: A tutorial extending Rails nested forms with Stimulus to support editing, deleting, and drag-and-drop repositioning of nested records. Covers adding a position column with a unique index, a generic RepositionController, updating the nested-fields Stimulus controller with a remove() method that handles both new and persisted records via _destroy, and a sortable Stimulus controller using SortableJS and @rails/request.js. Includes the full edit view ERB template wiring both controllers together.

recent_posts.title: Data Sovereignty: How to Keep All of Your Services in Europe (AppSignal + Hatchbox)
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to deploying Ruby on Rails applications on European infrastructure while maintaining GDPR compliance. Covers using Hatchbox (a PaaS-like deployment tool) with European cloud providers like Hetzner or Scaleway, combined with AppSignal (a Dutch APM/monitoring service) to keep all data — including application metrics, logs, and error tracking — within EU borders. Walks through server provisioning, app deployment, PostgreSQL/Redis setup, and AppSignal integration, with a discussion of trade-offs versus traditional approaches like Heroku or managed Kubernetes.

recent_posts.title: From Karafka Ractors to Yoichi Whisky: My RubyKaigi 2026 Experience
recent_posts.summary: A personal account of attending RubyKaigi 2026 in Hakodate, Hokkaido, covering key technical talks including Ruby namespacing (Box), JRuby history, next-gen GC, faster FFI, and the author's own talk on using Ractors in production with Karafka. Also includes reflections on the conference's role in bridging Japanese and Western Ruby communities, sponsored evening events, and an extended post-conference road trip through Hokkaido visiting onsens, distilleries, and historic sites.

recent_posts.title: How Rails Dispatches a Request to a Controller, and Why That Layer Matters
recent_posts.summary: Rails request handling is often simplified to 'route matches → action runs', but there is a significant dispatch layer in between. Once a route is matched, Rails must resolve the controller class, instantiate it, assemble request state, build params, and run callbacks before the action executes. Understanding this dispatch layer helps explain why before_action bugs and params confusion can be tricky — the problem often originates before the action body even starts. Key concepts covered include how Rails resolves controller strings like 'users#show' into actual classes, why each request gets a fresh controller instance, how params is assembled, and why render/redirect_to matter more than the action's Ruby return value.

recent_posts.title: Serving Rails frontend assets without an asset pipeline
recent_posts.summary: A Rails developer argues against using asset pipelines (Sprockets, propshaft, importmaps, Bun, webpack, etc.) for most web apps. The only real justification for asset fingerprinting is preventing mismatched assets during blue/green deployments — but this requires serving assets from a CDN anyway. Instead, the author proposes serving plain JS modules directly from the Rails app, using on-the-fly regex rewrites to append version query strings for cache busting, and scanning JS files at runtime to generate modulepreload link tags. The post advocates writing vanilla HTML, CSS, and JS with Stimulus controllers and web components, avoiding framework churn. It also warns against Bun due to its dropped support for older Intel Macs without AVX2, recommending esbuild instead.

recent_posts.title: Blue Ridge Ruby 2026 Recap
recent_posts.summary: A personal recap of the Blue Ridge Ruby 2026 conference in Asheville, covering talks from both days. Topics spanned permaculture analogies for sustainable software, Ruby procs vs lambdas, shipping large refactors, LLM telemetry in Rails, htmx with Hanami for e-ink devices, open-source contributions, and mindset/career growth strategies. The author also presented a talk on successful practices in an agentic world.

recent_posts.title: kamal-backup: Scheduled Rails Backups for Kamal Apps
recent_posts.summary: kamal-backup is a new open source Ruby gem and Docker image that provides scheduled, encrypted database and Active Storage backups for Rails apps deployed with Kamal. It uses restic under the hood for encryption, deduplication, and repository integrity checks. The tool supports PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB, and SQLite, and ships with a CLI covering setup, on-demand backups, restores, restore drills (including production-side scratch targets), and an evidence command that outputs redacted JSON suitable for security reviews. No cron setup or separate backup host is required — the Docker accessory handles scheduling internally.
